headerDisplay:
Split LIFX Ceiling uplight and downlight into two full-colour HomeKit lights. Local LAN control only — no LIFX cloud, no LIFX bridge.

**Works out of the box:** install it, and every LIFX Ceiling on the LAN (vendor 1, pid 176 US / pid 177 Intl) appears as two lights — Uplight and Downlight — each with full colour, brightness and colour-temperature control.

**The geometry is not configurable, on purpose.** On this product the uplight is driven by the **four corner cells** of the 8×8 matrix — `0, 7, 56, 63` — and the downlight by the other 60. Confirmed on four separate fixtures by painting cells and reading the panel, so it is a constant in `lib/matrix.js` (`CEILING_UPLIGHT_CELLS`), not a setting. A coloured dot inside the panel means one cell mis-assigned on that fixture — see `mappingFile`.

**Tile writes go out as service 715 with `ack_required: true`.** Un-acked frames vanish on this hardware with no error, so every write waits for its acknowledgement and treats service 223 as a failure.

**DHCP reservations are no longer required.** Accessory identity is the fixture's hardware MAC, persisted in the accessory cache, so a fixture that renews onto a new address keeps the same UUID, name and room — only its transport moves. A reservation is still *nice*: the logs stay tidy and reconnects are marginally faster.
footerDisplay: Both halves address the same physical fixture, so a fixture's power is only turned off when both halves are off.

aliases.title: Name aliases (MAC -> short name)
aliases.description: **Optional, site-local.** Short names for your fixtures: { "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff": "SW" } publishes "SW Uplight" and "SW Downlight". Keys are MACs — case and : separators are free — because a MAC survives an IP change. Unset, a tile is named from the label the fixture carries in the LIFX app, and a name you renamed in Home.app is left alone across restarts. Set an alias and it is republished every boot, because you asked for it. A key that is not a MAC is refused with a named warning.

mappingFile.title: Mapping file path
mappingFile.description: **Optional — repair only.** No file ships and none is needed: the verified corner model is compiled in. Set this to a JSON file of your own only if one fixture behaves differently, e.g. { "perDevice": { "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff": { "uplight": [0, 7, 56, 63], "downlight": [ … 60 indices … ] } } }. Keys are matched by normalised MAC, so case and separators do not matter; a `perDevice` entry outranks the file's global `uplight`/`downlight`, which outranks the built-in default. Anything that puts a lit cell inside the panel face shows up as visible dots — move that index into the other list instead of widening a radius.

kelvinMin.title: Minimum colour temperature (K)
kelvinMin.description: Warmest white the fixture will go. Clamped in software and published to HomeKit as the colour-temperature limit.

kelvinMax.title: Maximum colour temperature (K)
kelvinMax.description: Coolest white the fixture will go. Clamped in software and published to HomeKit as the colour-temperature limit.
